html:
Humayun's Tomb is the tomb of the second Mughal emperor, Humayun, in Delhi, built from 1565 to 1572. It was the first great garden tomb in India and the model for the Taj Mahal.

Humayun's widow Bega Begum paid for it, and a Persian architect, Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, designed it. It mixes Persian and Indian building ways:

  • It stands in a charbagh, a walled garden split into four by water channels, an image of paradise.
  • It is built of red sandstone with white marble trim.
  • It has a double dome: a high outer shell over a lower inner ceiling.

More than a hundred Mughal family members lie inside, which earned it the name "dormitory of the Mughals". In 1857, during the Indian Rebellion, the last emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, hid here before the British captured him.

It stands near the shrine of the Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya, and was restored in the 2000s. It is a World Heritage Site and one of the founding works of Mughal architecture.
sum: Humayun's Tomb is the tomb of the second Mughal emperor, Humayun, in Delhi, built from 1565 to 1572. It was the first great garden tomb in India and the model for the Taj Mahal.
